newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Alliance pivotal in NZ balance of power -Anderton.
newsitem.headline: Alliance pivotal in NZ balance of power -Anderton.

text.p: The left-wing Alliance Party still plays a pivotal role in deciding New Zealand's balance of power, leader Jim Anderton told Radio New Zealand on Monday.
"We (Alliance) have the votes. People haven't figured it out yet - if New Zealand First and Labour got into coalition, the Alliance has the numbers to ensure their legislation gets through or not.
"Everyone talks about the power that Winston Peters has at the present time."
But the only power Peters had was to decide between a conservative government and centre-left government, Anderton said.

The conservative National Party and its allies Act and United ended with 53 seats on Saturday against Labour and the Alliance's 50 leaving the nationalist New Zealand First with its 17 seats able to chose which grouping it sides with to rule.
If New Zealand First chooses Labour, they did not have the numbers to govern without Alliance support, Anderton said.
"The Alliance still plays a pivotal role. And with 13 MPs...we have an important part to play in the next 3 years."
Anderton also said many people, who supported the Alliance, chose Labour with their party vote.
"That came as a big surprise to me."
Alliance received 10.1 percent of the vote in Saturday's election, slumping from 18.2 percent in 1993.
